title: Realign and secure a robot conveyor's photoelectric detector
instruction: The conveyor detector is misaligned. Restore reliable detection and secure its mounting to the specified 3.0–3.5 N m tightening requirement. The supplied indicating torque wrench has a green 3.1-3.4 N m band within that requirement. Check detection with the orange test block, return it to its green pad, and leave the beam clear with both hands and the wrench away from the sensor.
context: Retroreflective detectors on conveyor rails provide object-position signals to robot cells. This maintenance operation restores a disturbed optical alignment, secures the actual adjustable mounting, and verifies that an opaque object switches the output after the robot releases the assembly.
setup: Fixed layout in metres: x away from arms, y left, z up. Two YAM parallel-jaw arms at (0,+/-0.305,0.75), 75 mm aperture, 40 N per finger. Wood table 1.10 x 1.30 x 0.06, top z=0.7475. Fixed steel conveyor frame 360 x 360 x 45 mm at (0.550,0.09,0.7700), rubber belt 330 x 340 x 3 mm at (0.555,0.09,0.7940). Steel pedestal 65 x 45 x 29 mm at (0.330,0.0273,0.7620), connected to frame by 70 x 45 x 6 mm bridge at (0.365,0.0273,0.7735). Vertical steel post diameter 12 x 60 mm at (0.330,0.0273,0.7890). Omron E39-L261 clamp: 23 x 42.3 x 23 mm body, 70 g, post axis (0.330,0.0273,0.8075), yaw -14 degrees, zero plate pitch; supplied 24 mm diameter x 5 mm plate, horizontal M5x15 screw with 8 mm AF nut. M5 reset tightening 0.10 +/-0.01 N m, with zero witness index. A custom steel adapter 30 x 4 x 24 mm joins this plate to the SICK-style bracket (30 x 23.5 x 2 mm foot; 2 x 19 x 46.5 mm upright). Blue 42 x 15.6 x 48.5 mm detector; plate, adapter, bracket and detector together 155 g. Sensor centre in bracket coordinates (31,0,25.25) mm; yellow 5 mm received-light indicator on top. Aligned bracket origin (0.330,0,0.8075); initial origin (0.323396,0.000811,0.8075). Fixed reflector 4 x 18 x 60 mm at (0.730,0,0.83275), on 12 x 18 x 59 mm post at (0.734,0,0.7770). Calibrated spring-indicating torque wrench (0-4 N m dial, accuracy +/-0.07 N m): 100 g socket/head and 120 g lever/grip; 8.1 mm AF socket, 12 mm depth, 0.3 mm bevel; square shaft 12 x 12 x 22 mm, spring head diameter 36 x 10 mm and 60 x 1 mm dial; 120 x 12 x 8 mm lever, rectangular 35 x 20 x 20 mm grip 120 mm from axis. The right gripper starts holding the wrench with its socket seated on the loose nut at 1.5 mm inward mouth depth, axis following the -14 degree clamp yaw, lever initially +z; grip centre 45 mm behind the mouth along its axis. Native torsion spring 10 N m/rad, visual pointer gearing 90 degrees/N m; green band 3.1-3.4 N m. Orange plastic test block 40 x 40 x 60 mm, 45 g at (0.250,0.180,0.7785), on fixed green 75 x 75 x 1 mm pad. Stationary isolated conveyor, powered detector and preset sensitivity are preconditions. Fixed RGB camera at (-0.12,0,0.87), aimed at (0.45,0,0.83); standard fixed-camera lens and standard left and right wrist cameras. The left hand starts clear at nominal TCP (0.16,0.40,0.9375).
scoring: Terminal score: 0.25 if the received-light LED is on. 0.5 additionally requires a valid fastening witness: with the socket seated and LED on, the calibrated dial stays in its 3.1-3.4 N m green band for at least 0.5 s while the nut changes at most 1 degree. The socket must contact only the nut, and the handle only the gripper; bracing the wrench against other objects or holding/blocking the nut directly cannot prove fastening. Then all robot parts and the tool must be >=5 mm clear of detector, plate, bracket and clamp. For 1.0, retain that released setting with LED on for 0.5 s, block the beam with the orange block alone for 0.5 s (LED off), and return/release the block wholly within its 75 mm pad, bottom within 3 mm of pad top, robot >=5 mm clear. These terminal conditions and LED on must hold for 10 consecutive 20 Hz steps. Regripping, tool contact or setting change >1 degree clears optical proof; loosening the nut >1 degree clears fastening proof. Otherwise 0.0. Permanently zero for frame tilt >15 degrees, dynamic objects leaving x=[-0.19,0.91], y=[-0.65,0.65], z=[0.7375,1.25], bracket separation >=2 mm, fixed frame/reflector movement >2 mm, indicated tool torque beyond 3.5 N m while engaged, or invalid shortcuts. During legitimate blockage current score is 0, with test history retained.
fidelity: Actual-size sensor and E39-L261 clamp with custom adapter. A native sliding key approximates seated hex engagement and releases on axial withdrawal; hands grasp by contact. A native spring and visible geared dial indicate torque. M5 compression and clamp friction are reduced estimates; thread and wiring geometry are omitted. Numerical calibration is separate from hardware measurement. A released optical test uses nine occlusion-tested rays.
scores: Dream-1 beta: 0.0 (1,200 steps); scripted RGB-only demo: 1.0 (1,034 steps, 10-step dwell). Seed 0, object jitter 0, 20 Hz.
reset_notes: Loosen the M5 nut, restore post height, yaw -14 degrees and plate pitch zero with a setup jig, then tighten to 0.10 +/-0.01 N m with a low-range calibrated instrument and mark zero. Seat the wrench on the nut and initialize the right gripper around its 20 mm grip, without attaching the tool to the hand; return the block. Simulation rebuilds all bodies, joints, views and cameras; restores poses and zero velocities; clears elastic-friction rest coordinates, nut/tool history and the dial pointer, torque witness and all optical/dwell counters. Seed 0, object jitter 0; no consumables.
